source_review.notes: Checked CNCF's current Platforms White Paper, DORA's platform guidance updated January 12, 2026 and corrected 2024 report, current Backstage Software Catalog, System Model, Entity Lifecycle, and Catalog Graph documentation, and Team Topologies. The chapter preserves the sources' distinctions among integrated capabilities, provider tools, catalog metadata, authoritative sources, caches, components, APIs, resources, and systems without claiming that a particular catalog product delivers platform outcomes.

evidence: Checked capability contract C_c=(U,J,I,O,S,G,R,L,E) and each consumer, job, intent, outcome, state, guarantee, responsibility, lifecycle, and evidence component.
Checked capability set C, tool/provider set T, relation M⊆C×T, forward provider set M(c), and inverse capability set M⁻¹(t).
Checked catalog tuple K_t=(id,type,a,p,o,s,f,d) and authority, provenance, owner, state, freshness, and domain metadata meanings.
Confirmed all notation uses GitHub-compatible math delimiters and distinguishes tuple labels from set names in prose.
notation_and_syntax.notes: The model supports traceability and does not assign numerical value to capabilities, tools, edges, or catalog records.

evidence: Confirmed three declared capabilities, four catalog tools, and five relation edges.
Confirmed deploy-service and issue-credential each compose two tools, with the explicit ascending-name tie-break selecting deploy-service.
Confirmed identity-provider and policy-engine each support two capabilities, with the explicit ascending-name tie-break selecting identity-provider.
Confirmed graph-database has zero mapped capabilities and is the only catalog-only tool.
Confirmed all six stdout lines exactly match the corrected annotation and generated report.
numerical_recomputation.notes: Counts describe a synthetic graph and do not measure consumer value, supportability, security, reliability, or capability fitness.

evidence: Traced each capability from consumer/job through intent, outcome, state, guarantees, responsibilities, lifecycle, and evidence independently of provider name.
Checked forward and inverse images of the many-to-many relation against the executable mapping.
Checked that catalog cardinality cannot entail capability cardinality or value because entries, providers, and contracts occupy different domains.
Checked that provider replacement entails compatibility review when consumer-observable contract semantics change.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: The relations establish topology and non-entailments, not correctness or optimal provider decomposition.

evidence: Reviewed catalog-only, capability-only, one-to-many, many-to-one, duplicate, stale, conflicting, ownerless, inaccessible, unavailable, deprecated, deleted, tombstoned, and transitive-provider cases.
Reviewed portal/CLI/API semantic drift, provider leakage, wrapper layers, automatic ingestion noise, manual-curation delay, hidden endorsement, search-ranking bias, and catalog/portal sprawl.
Reviewed provider failure, provider replacement, runtime/catalog disagreement, missing source entity, migration, support ambiguity, and retained underlying resources.
Reviewed clinical and national research-data examples with data-steward, legal, privacy, ethics, scientific, clinical, affected-community, and provider authority boundaries.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Scientific validity, clinical truth, lawful purpose, ethical acceptance, and affected-party legitimacy remain outside catalog or platform-mechanism authority.

evidence: Checked capability names and contracts remain outcome-oriented across provider and interface changes.
Checked accountable contract ownership despite multiple implementing teams and providers.
Checked field-level catalog authority, provenance, freshness, conflicts, support state, compatibility, and lifecycle.
Checked registration, search, access, authorization, fulfillment, readiness, operation, endorsement, and retirement remain distinct claims.
Checked capability and catalog lifecycles coordinate deletion without equating missing metadata with absent resources.
invariant_checking.notes: Concrete catalogs and capabilities still require schema, ingestion, authorization, search, conformance, reliability, accessibility, and operational evidence.

evidence: Reviewed the 500-tool portal counterexample disproving that catalog entries entail supported capabilities.
Reviewed the renamed provider wrapper counterexample disproving that an extra interface entails useful abstraction.
Reviewed scoped library approval disproving that a bare approved badge entails universal approval.
Reviewed deleted source metadata disproving that catalog absence entails resource retirement.
Confirmed the corrected executable graph establishes declared cardinality and tie-breaking only.
proof_review.notes: The chapter provides bounded arguments and counterexamples, not proof of catalog completeness, capability value, or provider substitutability.

evidence: Audited uses of capability, approved, endorsed, available, ready, supported, authoritative, source of truth, compatible, secure, complete, and current.
Confirmed claims carry consumer, workload, authority, source, scope, state, time, contract, or evidence boundaries.
Confirmed tool presence, graph edges, source guidance, registration, and internal review are not represented as proof of outcome or safety.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: The catalog is consistently described as composing or caching authoritative facts rather than becoming universal authority.

evidence: artifacts/snippets/PLAT-007/report.json records exact execution of capability-tool-graph under the captured Python 3 toolchain.
The initial run exposed a tie-break mismatch; the model was corrected to sort by descending count and ascending stable name before the passing reproduction.
Reproduced three capabilities, four tools, five edges, the two selected maxima, and one catalog-only tool.
Confirmed the chapter denies consumer fit, ownership, reliability, security, compatibility, support, or capability candidacy from the graph.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: Execution verifies deterministic topology and explicit tie-breaking only; it contains no production or user evidence.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed job-first capability design, complete contracts, tool/provider separation, ownership criteria, catalog data governance, bounded discovery claims, journey stages, many-to-many mapping, portal composition, lifecycle coordination, and separate outcome measures. The chapter preserves catalogs as valuable discovery/data products without confusing them with fulfillment and operation.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed CI link catalogs, provider wrappers, database portfolios, scoped approvals, ownership conflicts, shared dependency failures, search evidence, provider migration, disappearing entities, tombstones, portals, authoritative feeds, direct provider enablement, managed services, and clinical/research data. Each scenario assigns consumer, platform, provider, catalog, and domain responsibilities.

pedagogical_review.notes: The objectives align with ten distinct examples and five exercises progressing from classification through contract design, authority matrices, provider strategy comparison, and national research-data transfer. Answers provide complete models and explicit claim boundaries.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external academic or practitioner review is claimed.
